question: Shared on the printed figures, not on the record's framing. Both papers estimate the association of antihypertensive drug use with progression from MCI to dementia in older adults with MCI, from clinical medication records (the clinical/cognitive/questionnaire channel). The record sets P-999's per-class HRs against P-1157's polypharmacy HR (0.49). Polypharmacy (5 or more drugs) is a different named factor, so that alignment fails condition 1. The alignment that shares the factor is P-1157's 'Antihypertensive Drugs' category against P-999's 'any AHM vs no AHM'. P-1157's Figure 3 lists 'Antihypertensive Drugs' as one pooled category among its 15 ATC categories, with no separate diuretic, beta-blocker, CCB or RAS category (read from the figure image by in-memory OCR). Allowed differences, recorded as candidate explanations: P-999 restricts to hypertensive MCI, so its reference group is untreated hypertensives, while P-1157 includes normotensive participants; also data source and country, exposure window, outcome ascertainment, covariate set and sample size.
metric: Adjusted Cox hazard ratio with adjusted Cox hazard ratio (match); direction of association with direction of association.

figures.P-999: Any AHM users vs AHM non-users, incident ADRD after first MCI diagnosis, hypertensive MCI, N = 128,683 (100,678 vs 28,005): aHR 1.06 (95% CI 1.04-1.08), P < 0.001, as printed (Table 3). The per-class estimates against non-users of that class (who may take other classes) are 0.96-0.98, upper bounds 0.98-1.00. Strata: with statins 0.84 (0.80-0.88), without statins 1.11 (1.08-1.13); with metformin 0.86 (0.76-0.96), without metformin 1.06 (1.04-1.08).
figures.P-1157: Baseline exposure to antihypertensive drugs vs no exposure, progression from CDR 0.5 to CDR 1 (neurologist-confirmed dementia), N = 237 (89 progressed): HR 0.59 (95% CI 0.37-0.93), as printed. Adjusted for age, sex, CCI, education, smoking, hearing and visual impairment, Barthel, GDS-15, MNA-SF and recruitment source. (Polypharmacy HR 0.49, 0.31-0.78, is a different factor and is not compared.)

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists. P-1157 reports no antihypertensive HR within its 154 hypertensive participants (P-999's population condition), and no hypertension-adjusted or co-medication-adjusted per-category model. P-999 reports no analysis that includes normotensive MCI patients, and none with baseline-only exposure. P-999's statin and metformin strata are not P-1157's condition, since P-1157 is not restricted by co-medication. They do not reconcile the pair in any case: the most favourable stratum, 0.84 (0.80-0.88), still excludes P-1157's 0.59, although 0.84 lies inside P-1157's interval. The gap is therefore not dissolved by either paper's own data.
performance_validity: Not a performance comparison (observational association estimates); condition 5 does not apply.

candidate_explanations.difference: Population and reference group. P-999 is restricted to hypertensive MCI, so AHM users are compared with untreated hypertensives. P-1157 includes normotensive MCI participants, so its unexposed group mixes normotensives with untreated hypertensives, and it has no hypertension covariate. P-1157 also finds hypertension more common among non-progressors (72.3% vs 52.8%), and P-999 names this confounder as the reason it excluded normotensives.
candidate_explanations.quote: including normotensive patients with MCI to our population would add a potential confounder (hypertension status) that could not be well controlled as very few normotensive patients are taking AHMs.

candidate_explanations.difference: Hypertension is associated with non-progression within P-1157's cohort, so AHM exposure there may partly stand in for hypertension status.
candidate_explanations.quote: participants who progressed to dementia had a lower prevalence of hypertension (p = 0.003)

candidate_explanations.difference: Co-medication adjustment. P-999's model is adjusted for statin and metformin use, and its AHM estimate changes direction with statin co-use (0.84 with, 1.11 without). P-1157's per-category models adjust for no other medication, and lipid-modifying drugs are separately protective in its data (HR 0.43).
candidate_explanations.quote: Under consumption of Statins, use of any AHMs or major AHM classes except for ‘Other’ AHMs showed protective effect against ADRD risk, whereas the use showed harmful effect under non-consumption of Statins.

candidate_explanations.difference: Exposure window. P-1157 uses baseline prescription records, while P-999 classifies use over the study period.
candidate_explanations.quote: Based on baseline prescription records in our cohort, we identified the 15 most commonly prescribed medication categories for subsequent analysis.
The study included 100,678 patients who were taking at least one class of AHM and 28,005 who were not taking any AHMs during the study period.

candidate_explanations.difference: Outcome ascertainment. P-999 identifies ADRD from claims ICD codes or two anti-dementia drug fills within 6 months. P-1157 uses an annual CDR change from 0.5 to 1 confirmed by neurologists.
candidate_explanations.quote: Progression from MCI to dementia was defined as an increase in the CDR score from 0.5 to 1 during follow-up. Dementia diagnoses were further confirmed by the neurologists

candidate_explanations.difference: Data source, setting and size. P-999 uses US Optum commercial claims (N = 128,683; a preprint whose Methods print COPD ICD codes as the hypertension definition, an evident transcription error). P-1157 is a Taiwanese veterans cohort mixing institutionalised residents and outpatients (N = 237).
candidate_explanations.quote: our cohort included both institutionalized residents and community-dwelling outpatients.

candidate_explanations.difference: Multiplicity. P-1157's antihypertensive estimate is one of 15 exploratory per-category Cox models, tested at p < 0.05 without correction.
candidate_explanations.quote: additional Cox regression analyses were conducted for the 15 most commonly prescribed medication categories based on the ATC classification system.

reason: On the figures the papers print for the same factor, antihypertensive use and progression from MCI to dementia, the estimates point in opposite significant directions and their intervals do not overlap: P-1157 HR 0.59 (0.37-0.93) against P-999 aHR 1.06 (1.04-1.08). No figure in either paper under the other's condition reconciles them, so the pair qualifies as an unresolved discrepancy. The record's own framing (per-class 0.96-0.98 against polypharmacy 0.49) compares different factors and misreads P-999's comparator, and it would not qualify. The candidate explanations are the reference-group and population difference (untreated hypertensives against a mixed group that includes normotensives), co-medication adjustment, exposure window, outcome ascertainment, setting and multiplicity. Neither paper shows any of them to be sufficient.

quotes.quote: Patients who use any form of AHMs had 6% higher adjusted hazard ratio of ADRD (95% CI: (1.04, 1.08), P < 0.001) than non-users (Table 3).

‘AHM users’ refer to patients consuming at least one antihypertensive medication according to the WHOCC ATC classification system, whereas ‘AHM non-users’ refer to patients who do not take any form of antihypertensive medications.
the study population was narrowed down from patients with Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) to hypertensive patients with MCI.
